purpose.business: Load/refresh waiver reserve detail rows (reserve type = 'W') into the fact table FCT_LG_RESERVE_DETAILS_R for a specific reserve valuation cycle using staging input STG_WAIVER_RESERVES_R and prior-month fact rows to compute change values.
purpose.technical: Incremental load that (a) determines the current valuation cycle from DIM_TIME_R and STG_WAIVER_RESERVES_R, (b) deletes existing waiver rows for that valuation date from FCT_LG_RESERVE_DETAILS_R, and (c) INSERTs new/updated rows by full-outer-joining current staging values with prior-month fact rows to calculate deltas and populate the fact table. Also writes a debug/log row at the end.

purpose.business: Propagate reinsurance party and percentage information from a staging feed (group reinsurer claim percent) to multiple claim payment fact/detail tables so reporting and downstream MV tables reflect primary/secondary/ternary reinsurer IDs and reinsurance percentage/share fields.
purpose.technical: Calculate prior and current fiscal boundary dates from DIM_TIME_R based on input batch id, then run a series of MERGE ... WHEN MATCHED THEN UPDATE statements to update multiple FCT_* tables from STG_GRP_REINSURER_CLAIM_PCT_R and one downstream MV table from an updated FCT table. Commits are issued after each MERGE. Basic exception capture exists for the last block.

The FCT_CLAIM_PAYMENT_DETAIL_BENEFIT_PAYMENT_R table is updated then read once later in the procedure.

conditional mapping (CASE to null secondary/ternary when pct < 0)

MERGE-based updates (MATCHED -> UPDATE) to multiple target tables

MERGE (UPDATE only) FCT_CLAIM_PAYMENT_DETAIL_EXPENSE_R from STG_GRP_REINSURER_CLAIM_PCT_R (no date filter). COMMIT.

MAIN: call FN_GET_PACS_BATCH_ASOF_DT and store gd_pacs_batch_asof_dt.

OPTIMIZATION_SIGNALS.direct_copy_vs_derived_logic: Large portion of columns are near pass-through from source MVs and dims (direct copy); derived fields (CASE mappings, date conversions) are fewer but repeated. The pass-through nature indicates good candidates for hop reduction by removing intermediate updates/merges.

HOP_REDUCTION_OPPORTUNITIES.current_pattern: INSERT INTO RPT_CLAIM_DTL_R (INSERT SELECT) -> MERGE to update N_ANY_OCC_DAYS_REMAINING_R
HOP_REDUCTION_OPPORTUNITIES.recommended_action: Compute N_ANY_OCC_DAYS_REMAINING_R in the initial INSERT SELECT (use expression D_ANY_OCC_START_DATE_R - (SYSDATE-1)) and remove the MERGE.
HOP_REDUCTION_OPPORTUNITIES.reason: Derived value depends only on D_ANY_OCC_START_DATE_R and current sysdate; folding saves a full scan/merge over inserted rows.

HOP_REDUCTION_OPPORTUNITIES.current_pattern: INSERT SELECT already selects D_PRD_R via join -> later UPDATE sets D_PRD_R from CLAIM_TIER_WFAM_MV_TBL
HOP_REDUCTION_OPPORTUNITIES.recommended_action: Ensure the correct D_PRD_R value is selected during the INSERT (remove the later UPDATE) or consolidate the logic to a single join/selection; if timing/snapshot issues exist, consider snapshotting CLAIM_TIER_WFAM_MV_TBL consistently before INSERT.
HOP_REDUCTION_OPPORTUNITIES.reason: Avoids another scan/update on target; moderate risk if there are snapshot/timing differences between insert and update sources.

HOP_REDUCTION_OPPORTUNITIES.current_pattern: main's large SELECT duplicated in prc_get_cur_data (main -> prc_get_cur_data)
HOP_REDUCTION_OPPORTUNITIES.recommended_action: Expose the large query as a single reusable view/materialized view or a single procedure that returns a ref cursor; have main call that instead of duplicating SQL.
HOP_REDUCTION_OPPORTUNITIES.reason: High maintainability improvement and eliminates redundant parsing and optimization overhead.

HOP_REDUCTION_OPPORTUNITIES.current_pattern: prc_upd_del_data deletes rows using EXISTS against a derived subquery which scans dim_grp_claim_dir_r (with same threshold used later in insert)
HOP_REDUCTION_OPPORTUNITIES.issue_type: duplicate source scans and procedural chaining
HOP_REDUCTION_OPPORTUNITIES.recommended_action: Compute the list of affected keys once (in a CTE or temporary table) and reuse it for DELETE and the INSERT filtering; or push delete logic into a single set-based MERGE that handles changed rows.
HOP_REDUCTION_OPPORTUNITIES.reason: Reduces repeated scans of dim_grp_claim_dir_r and prevents multiple passes over large source tables.

HOP_REDUCTION_OPPORTUNITIES.current_pattern: prc_trunc_partition does DDL then immediate index rebuilds, and later PKG_GRP_COMMON_UTIL.prc_rebuild_index_partitions is also invoked
HOP_REDUCTION_OPPORTUNITIES.recommended_action: Clarify responsibilities: either do full partition truncate + index rebuild in one centralized utility or avoid rebuilding the same indexes twice. Use consistent parallel degree settings.
HOP_REDUCTION_OPPORTUNITIES.reason: Index rebuilds are I/O/CPU heavy; duplicate rebuilds waste resources.

structural_improvements: Centralize the large SELECT logic into a single database object: a view (if acceptable) or a single parameterized stored function that returns a ref cursor. This eliminates duplication between main and prc_get_cur_data and simplifies maintenance.
Introduce a small lookup table or a deterministic function for the long UPPER(t.v_event_cause_r) -> code mapping to avoid repeating the CASE block multiple times.
sql_optimization_ideas: Fold post-load MERGE/UPDATE logic into the INSERT SELECT where possible (compute derived columns at insert time).

Avoid repeated full scans by capturing the incremental threshold (SELECT max(END_DATE) ...) into a local variable once and then reusing that variable in subsequent SQL statements instead of re-running the scalar subquery.

Replace EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM (SELECT ... FROM dim_grp_claim_dir_r ...)) structure with a direct EXISTS with appropriate indexed predicates or a WITH list of affected keys to reduce nested subquery overhead.
Reduce frequent COMMITs: batch logging writes or use fewer transactional commits so the main insert/update can run in a single transaction (subject to rollback/operational policy).
data_model_improvements: Where repeated CASE mappings are used, convert them to small reference lookup tables (normalized mapping) and join in the mapping at query time â€” allows easier updates and can be indexed.
If performance critical, consider a materialized view for the heavy join of the core claim domains (refreshed as appropriate) so the large INSERT can read from a pre-joined flattened structure.
modularization_suggestions: Expose one main entry point (main) and reduce public surface area: keep small reusable helpers for logging, partition maintenance, and error handling.

Refactor prc_get_cur_data to call the same centralized query (function/view) used by main rather than duplicating SQL. If prc_get_cur_data is only returning what main already computes, consider removing it.
REFACTORING_RECOMMENDATIONS.package_recommendation: Keep this package as the orchestration coordinator (main) but extract the large, reused SELECT into a separate reusable object (view or table function). Do not keep duplicated SQL across child procedures; convert repeated helpers into a shared utility module.
REFACTORING_RECOMMENDATIONS.commit_and_logging: Minimize logging COMMITs; batch log inserts or mark logs to be written at the end where operationally safe to reduce commit overhead during heavy DML.

purpose.business: Load and maintain the RPT_CLAIM_SUM_R reporting table (monthly claim summary rows) and provide procedures to populate and update derived amount/reserve/indicator columns.
purpose.technical: Provide procedures to (a) build an exchange staging table and bulk-insert current-month data (prc_get_cur_data), (b) orchestrate run steps including creating exchange table, partition-exchange into the production table and gather stats (MAIN), and (c) perform multiple set/bulk updates against the reporting table to populate amount, reserve and derived fields using PL/SQL bulk-collect / FORALL patterns (prc_upd_cols). Uses parallel DML, partition exchange, mview refresh, and DBMS_STATS.

However n_current_face_amount_r depends on class_of_business from RPT_POLICY_DTL_R_CLASSOFBUS_MV_SSL which the code refreshes in prc_upd_cols; that MV is refreshed after the main load in the current flow, so the class_of_business value is not available at initial insert in the current sequence. Therefore some columns are not derivable at insert time with the present ordering.

procedure_level_flow.prc_get_cur_data: Enables parallel DML, inserts a set-based SELECT (many LEFT JOINs and a grouped subquery) into RPT_CLAIM_SUM_R_EXG, commits, then disables parallel DML; logs rowcounts.
procedure_level_flow.MAIN: Orchestrates logging, fiscal period calculations, creates exchange table, calls prc_get_cur_data, performs partition exchange into RPT_CLAIM_SUM_R, rebuilds indexes on the new partition, conditionally gathers table stats on month-end, and logs completion.
procedure_level_flow.prc_upd_cols: Separate procedure that (a) computes/updates payment amount columns by bulk-collecting from RPT_CLAIM_PAYMENT_DTL_AMT_MV_SSL and FORALL updating RPT_CLAIM_SUM_R, (b) computes reserve aggregates from RPT_RESERVE_DETAILS_R and FORALL updates RPT_CLAIM_SUM_R, (c) refreshes the RPT_POLICY_DTL_R_CLASSOFBUS_MV_SSL materialized view, and (d) computes current face amount in PL/SQL by scanning RPT_CLAIM_SUM_R and updating it by ROWID. Uses repeated commits per batch. This procedure is the main data-derivation executor; MAIN does not call it inside this body (it is separate).

procedure_specific_signals.opportunities_to_merge_child_procedures: prc_upd_cols contains several logically related update steps that could be consolidated into a smaller set of set-based UPDATE/MERGE statements rather than multiple cursor+FORALL blocks and row-by-row PL/SQL logic.

cross_procedure_duplicates.consolidation_recommendation: Combine some of the update logic (payments, reserves) into the initial INSERT SELECT (LEFT JOIN aggregated payment/reserve subqueries) or perform a single MERGE/UPDATE that sets all derived columns in one pass. If class_of_business MV must be refreshed, refresh it before the main INSERT so the initial load can derive n_current_face_amount_r.

HOP_REDUCTION_OPPORTUNITIES.current_pattern: INSERT (prc_get_cur_data) -> PARTITION_EXCHANGE (MAIN) -> multiple UPDATE passes (prc_upd_cols)
HOP_REDUCTION_OPPORTUNITIES.recommended_action: Refresh dependencies (materialized view) and fold payment/reserve lookups and class_of_business logic into the initial INSERT SELECT or into a single set-based MERGE so that fewer update passes are required.
HOP_REDUCTION_OPPORTUNITIES.reason: Reduces I/O and repeated scans of the large target table and removes repeated FORALL/commit cycles. Requires verification that RPT_* sources / MV are available up-front and that partition exchange semantics are preserved.

HOP_REDUCTION_OPPORTUNITIES.current_pattern: PL/SQL rowset compute: SELECT RPT_CLAIM_SUM_R (cursor cur_upd_data) -> PL/SQL loop compute class_of_business logic -> UPDATE RPT_CLAIM_SUM_R by ROWID
HOP_REDUCTION_OPPORTUNITIES.recommended_action: Replace row-by-row PL/SQL logic with a single set-based UPDATE joining RPT_POLICY_DTL_R_CLASSOFBUS_MV_SSL (or use CASE in SQL) to compute n_current_face_amount_r in SQL, avoiding the SELECT-then-UPDATE loop.
HOP_REDUCTION_OPPORTUNITIES.reason: Same-table cursor update is the strongest candidate for folding into a single set-based update; logic is primarily set-based conditions that can be expressed as CASE/joins.

HOP_REDUCTION_OPPORTUNITIES.current_pattern: Multiple FORALL update blocks each committing per batch
HOP_REDUCTION_OPPORTUNITIES.recommended_action: Consolidate FORALL updates where possible into fewer FORALL operations or a single set-based MERGE; reduce commits frequency (commit after larger batches or at transaction end if acceptable).
HOP_REDUCTION_OPPORTUNITIES.reason: Lower redo/undo and improve throughput; must consider undo/transaction size and recovery requirements.

HOP_REDUCTION_OPPORTUNITIES.current_pattern: Materialized view refresh (RPT_POLICY_DTL_R_CLASSOFBUS_MV_SSL) performed inside prc_upd_cols
HOP_REDUCTION_OPPORTUNITIES.recommended_action: Refresh this MV prior to initial INSERT so its values can be joined during the insert and eliminate the need for later MV-dependent updates.
HOP_REDUCTION_OPPORTUNITIES.reason: MV refresh cost may be high but moving it earlier can enable set-based insertion of derived column; must ensure data correctness (consistency of MV with other reporting inputs).

structural_improvements: Consider making MAIN the single end-to-end entrypoint that invokes prc_get_cur_data and prc_upd_cols in the required order (or document/automate external orchestration) to ensure consistent runs.
Centralize repeated logging calls into a small wrapper to reduce duplication.
sql_optimization_ideas: Move payment and reserve aggregates into the main INSERT SELECT as LEFT JOINed subqueries (aggregates grouped by keys) to avoid separate payment/reserve update passes.
Replace the PL/SQL loop that computes n_current_face_amount_r with a single set-based UPDATE using CASE/DECODE or a JOIN to the refreshed RPT_POLICY_DTL_R_CLASSOFBUS_MV_SSL MV.
If RPT_POLICY_DTL_R_CLASSOFBUS_MV_SSL can be refreshed beforehand, include its join in the initial insert to set n_current_face_amount_r directly.
Reduce commit frequency inside bulk loops; perform commits at larger logical boundaries or after full FORALL completion to improve transactional throughput.
data_model_improvements: If RPT_ intermediate reporting tables (payments, reserves, policy-class-of-business) are stable and used frequently together, consider consolidating pre-aggregations into stable summary tables that can be cheaply joined at load time.
modularization_suggestions: Refactor prc_upd_cols into smaller set-based update procedures (e.g., update_payments, update_reserves, update_face_amount) or collapse them into a single set-based updater. Extract common key predicates to shared helper functions if needed.
Keep MAIN as the coordinator but ensure it triggers the entire end-to-end process (including prc_upd_cols) to minimize manual orchestration steps.
REFACTORING_RECOMMENDATIONS.package_recommendation: Keep the package as an orchestrator with small reusable helpers, but refactor prc_upd_cols to reduce procedural complexity. Do not split the package unless there is a strong ownership/permission reason; instead flatten and consolidate closely related update logic into set-based operations within this package.

purpose.business: Populate and maintain the monthly reporting table RPT_POLICY_DTL_R (policy-level reporting facts) for the current reporting month, including loading current data, partition-exchanging into the report table, and filling numerous derived and lookup columns.

The package also uses GTT DIM_PLAN_DESIGN_DIRECTORY_R_GTT to stage plan design data used by subsequent updates, and logs progress via shared logging utilities.

PERFORMANCE_CHARACTERISTICS.parallelism_usage: Yes - package enables parallel DML in sessions (ALTER SESSION ENABLE PARALLEL DML) and index rebuild requests with p_parallel_degree => 8.
PERFORMANCE_CHARACTERISTICS.partition_usage: Yes - partition-exchange is used to swap the exchange table into the monthly partition of RPT_POLICY_DTL_R.
PERFORMANCE_CHARACTERISTICS.bulk_operations: Yes - extensive use of BULK COLLECT and FORALL in PRC_UPD_COL_DETAILS with a bulk limit (gn_bulk_coll_cnt = 50000).
PERFORMANCE_CHARACTERISTICS.heavy_joins_or_subqueries: Yes - the initial insert (prc_get_cur_data) contains many joins, window functions (RANK), ranked subqueries and max-timestamp subqueries. Many cursors also have aggregated group-by logic.
potential_bottlenecks: Multiple, sequential update passes over the same target partition (RPT_POLICY_DTL_R) cause repeated full/partial scans and significant redo/undo and IO.
Frequent COMMIT inside update loops increases redo and may reduce performance (many small transactions).
DIM_PLAN_DESIGN_DIRECTORY_R_GTT is read many times; if populated as a persisted table it may be expensive to scan repeatedly.
Many correlated EXISTS queries on RPT_POLICY_DTL_R in sources add nested-loop style overhead.
Per-row date parsing logic (SELECT TO_DATE(...) INTO ld_theft_dt) inside a loop over a bulk collection results in PL/SQL per-row work instead of pure set-based SQL.

OPTIMIZATION_SIGNALS.duplicate_logic: Numerous repeated cursor patterns and update loops with identical structure (SELECT -> BULK COLLECT -> FORALL UPDATE -> COMMIT).
OPTIMIZATION_SIGNALS.redundant_joins: Multiple EXISTS checks against RPT_POLICY_DTL_R across different cursors. The same joins between DIM_GRP_POLICY_DIR_R and FCT_GRP_POLICY_R appear multiple places.
OPTIMIZATION_SIGNALS.pass_through_transformations: Many columns are inserted as NULL in prc_get_cur_data and then immediately populated by PRC_UPD_COL_DETAILS — this is near pass-through: the data exists in other tables and could often be joined at INSERT time.
OPTIMIZATION_SIGNALS.staging_tables_that_can_be_removed: DIM_PLAN_DESIGN_DIRECTORY_R_GTT is heavily reused across updates; while it cannot necessarily be eliminated without redesign, its population could be integrated earlier or the logic applied during initial insert to avoid the extra write-read hop.
OPTIMIZATION_SIGNALS.repeated_transformation_patterns: Repeated group-by and aggregation over fct_plan_design_summary_r joined to DIM_PLAN_DESIGN_DIRECTORY_R_GTT for different coverage codes — same base join with only coverage_code filter changing.
OPTIMIZATION_SIGNALS.unnecessary_full_loads: If only subset of columns needs post-population, some updates could be merged into a single UPDATE/MERGE; multiple passes are likely avoidable.
OPTIMIZATION_SIGNALS.high_cost_joins: Rank/window queries and max-time subqueries over large FCT tables (FCT_GRP_TRANSACTIONS_R and FCT_GRP_BILLING_POLICY_DTL_R) are high cost.

package_specific_duplicates.duplicate_sql_blocks_across_child_proced: Yes. Multiple cursors select from FCT_PLAN_DESIGN_SUMMARY_R join DIM_PLAN_DESIGN_DIRECTORY_R_GTT with varying coverage_code filters (e.g. IDTHEFT, IDTHEFTEFFDATE, PSINDICATOR, ELIMPERIOD, EAP/EAP_EFF_DATE, BEREAVE/BEREAVEDATE).
package_specific_duplicates.repeated_partition_index_maintenance: Index rebuild is called centrally for the partition; repeated calls are not obvious within package but index maintenance is externalized.
package_specific_duplicates.repeated_logging_or_commits: Extensive and repeated logging for each step (many prc_ins_prcs_job_log_message_r calls) and COMMIT after every FORALL batch.
package_specific_duplicates.merge_child_procedures_opportunity: Several cursor/update blocks share similar source joins and WHERE predicates and should be consolidated into parameterized SQL blocks or combined set-based updates.

consolidation_recommendations: Merge many small cursor/update iterations into a few set-based UPDATE ... FROM / MERGE statements joining the target to the source aggregates, reducing multiple scans of the target.
Fold derivable columns into the initial INSERT into RPT_POLICY_DTL_R_EXG (or perform single MERGE after exchange) to eliminate most post-load updates.
Parameterize repeated plan-design queries (coverage code) and run a single aggregated query returning columns for all coverages, pivoting/conditionalizing in SQL instead of separate cursor loops.
Reduce number of commits: commit per larger batch or at logical boundaries to reduce redo churn, keeping bulk limits appropriate for undo/redo constraints.

HOP_REDUCTION_OPPORTUNITIES.current_pattern: prc_get_cur_data (INSERT -> RPT_POLICY_DTL_R_EXG) -> PARTITION_EXCHANGE -> PRC_UPD_COL_DETAILS (multiple update passes on RPT_POLICY_DTL_R)
HOP_REDUCTION_OPPORTUNITIES.recommended_action: Push as many derived columns as possible into the initial INSERT (join in prc_get_cur_data) or build a single MERGE/UPDATE that populates many columns in one set-based pass instead of many cursor updates.
HOP_REDUCTION_OPPORTUNITIES.reason: Most update sources are available at load time; folding reduces repeated scans and I/O. Risk moderate because logic is complex and requires careful validation.

HOP_REDUCTION_OPPORTUNITIES.current_pattern: Many individual cursor BULK_COLLECT -> FORALL UPDATE loops (each updating one or a few columns)
HOP_REDUCTION_OPPORTUNITIES.recommended_action: Consolidate related cursor updates into fewer SQL statements (single MERGE or multi-column UPDATE with joins) or at least group updates that read the same source dataset.
HOP_REDUCTION_OPPORTUNITIES.reason: Mechanical consolidation reduces context-switching, reduces commits and I/O; low functional risk if logic grouped carefully and tested.

HOP_REDUCTION_OPPORTUNITIES.current_pattern: DIM_PLAN_DESIGN_DIRECTORY_R -> DIM_PLAN_DESIGN_DIRECTORY_R_GTT (write) -> many reads by cursors
HOP_REDUCTION_OPPORTUNITIES.recommended_action: Either (a) perform plan-design filtering inline during the initial insert; or (b) populate the staging once but transform/aggregate into a single temp result set consumed by the updates to avoid repeated scans.
HOP_REDUCTION_OPPORTUNITIES.reason: GTT is read many times; consolidating reduces I/O but requires rewrite of dependent cursor logic.

HOP_REDUCTION_OPPORTUNITIES.current_pattern: PL/SQL per-row parsing of dates inside a loop (TO_DATE in PL/SQL loop) for D_ID_THEFT_DATE_R
HOP_REDUCTION_OPPORTUNITIES.recommended_action: Convert parsing/formatting to set-based SQL (update using TO_DATE in SQL or handle in initial insert) to remove per-row PL/SQL SELECT INTO in a loop.
HOP_REDUCTION_OPPORTUNITIES.reason: Set-based elimination is straightforward and yields immediate CPU and context-switch improvements.

HOP_REDUCTION_OPPORTUNITIES.current_pattern: Many EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM RPT_POLICY_DTL_R WHERE ...) filters across cursors after insert
HOP_REDUCTION_OPPORTUNITIES.issue_type: redundant existence checks and repeated scans on target
HOP_REDUCTION_OPPORTUNITIES.recommended_action: Use a single keyed temporary list of policy_sks present in the new partition (or use the exchange table directly) and join to that set instead of repeated EXISTS against the live table.
HOP_REDUCTION_OPPORTUNITIES.reason: Reduces repeated index lookups on the target; simple to implement as it leverages the exchange table rowset.

structural_improvements: Expose 'main' as the single public entry point; collapse internal procedures into clear responsibilities: 'extract_load', 'exchange_partition', 'rebuild_indexes', 'enrich_data'.
Split PRC_UPD_COL_DETAILS into smaller set-based enrichment modules grouped by data source (e.g., plan-design derived columns, underwriting derived columns, agency/agent derived columns).
sql_optimization_ideas: Fold derivable columns into the initial INSERT select (prc_get_cur_data) to remove many update passes.
Replace multiple cursor BULK_COLLECT/FORALL loops with indexed MERGE or UPDATE ... FROM (set-based joins + aggregated subqueries).
Use analytic/aggregate SQL to produce all plan-design derived columns in a single pass (pivot or conditional aggregation by coverage_code) rather than separate group-bys per coverage_code.
Avoid per-row PL/SQL parsing (TO_DATE in loop); perform conversions in SQL or use deterministic conversion functions during initial load.
Reduce COMMIT frequency to larger batches but ensure undo/redo constraints are respected; or allow the DB to manage transactions when doing set-based operations.
data_model_improvements: If many updates rely on DIM_PLAN_DESIGN_DIRECTORY rows linked to policies for the same month, consider a persisted pre-joined summary table refreshed once per run to be used by all update steps.
Ensure appropriate indexes exist on join/filter columns used by heavy joins (n_policy_sk_r, n_yearmonth_r, n_plan_design_sk_r, n_policy_id_r) to reduce repeated full scans.
modularization_suggestions: Retain package as coordinator (main) but move heavy set-based data movement into distinct PL/SQL procedures or even separate SQL scripts that can be executed as single set-based statements.
Expose a small set of helper functions/procedures for repeated logic (e.g., build_plan_design_summary(coverage_codes), build_cross_sell_summary(month)) to avoid duplication.
REFACTORING_RECOMMENDATIONS.package_splitting_guidance: Keep the package as a coordinator but refactor PRC_UPD_COL_DETAILS: either split it into several specialized enrichment procedures or convert it into a single set-based enrichment routine. The package should expose 'main' plus a few small reusable helpers rather than many near-duplicate child procedures.

purpose.business: Populate and maintain the RPT_CLAIM_DTL_R reporting partition for the current fiscal month (load claim-detail rows, ensure prior month rows inactivated, produce indicator/decision columns and flags).
purpose.technical: Orchestrates partition-level truncation, bulk-load of claim detail rows from many DIM/FACT/MV sources using a REF CURSOR -> BULK COLLECT -> FORALL INSERT, then runs post-load updates (indicator flags and decision/turnaround columns), index rebuilds and tiny housekeeping inserts (dummy record).

SCRIPT_METADATA.load_type: mixed (partition-level full load for current month with post-load incremental updates/flags)

package_details.package_role: Mostly orchestration (ETL/load coordinator) with some embedded business logic and small utility functions

does_actual_data_movement: prc_get_cur_data (produces the source cursor used by main for inserts)
only_setup_cleanup_orchestration: prc_upd_del_data (decides truncation vs prior-month inactivation and calls prc_trunc_partition)

OTHER: rpt_claim_dtl_r (target also referenced as source in some procs)

external_dependencies: global package variables and constants referenced (gn_current_month, gn_sysdt_batchid, gc_* etc.) are external to this body (from package spec).

same_tables_used_repeatedly: rpt_claim_dtl_r (target, also read by prc_upd_decision_cols and used to compute post-load aggregates)
many DIM_/MV_ objects used repeatedly in prc_get_cur_data
ALL_INDEXES is queried in two places (prc_trunc_partition and prc_rebuild_indexes)

prc_trunc_partition: ALL_INDEXES (to rebuild PK indexes after truncation)
prc_get_cur_data: a long list of DIM/MV/FACT tables described above (dim_grp_claim_dir_r, dim_grp_claim_coverage_r, MVW_PRODUCT_SK_LOOKUP_MIN_MV_SSL, CLAIM_TIER_WFAM_MV_TBL, multiple MV and FACT subqueries)
prc_rebuild_indexes: ALL_INDEXES (rebuild non-PK unusable indexes for RPT_CLAIM_DTL_R)
prc_upd_decision_cols: rpt_claim_dtl_r (used in source join and update target)
rpt_claim_dtl_r_claimdec_GTT (GTT staging used to hold aggregated rows before FORALL updates)

priority_repeated_scans_filters_lookups: Repeated scan/read of rpt_claim_dtl_r (insert then updates then read for decision cols);
Repeated event_cause -> code mapping CASE block duplicated inside prc_get_cur_data (same mapping appears twice)
Repeated index metadata scans (ALL_INDEXES) in two procedures

transformation_types: filters (active status filters like v_active_status_r='Y', many NVL/CASE guards)
aggregations (GROUP BY / MAX used in prc_upd_decision_cols and subqueries)
bulk insert (FORALL) and cursor-based updates (FORALL + bulk collect)
repeated_logic_blocks: Event-cause CASE -> code mapping block appears twice (identical mapping used to decide which elimination period to pick).
Two similar cursor->FORALL update patterns in prc_upd_wavier_ltd_ind_cols (one for LTD, one for WOP) follow the same structure.

hardcoded_logic.column: V_EVENT_CAUSE_R (mapped to elimination-code aliases inside CASE expressions)
hardcoded_logic.notes: This large CASE appears twice in the main prc_get_cur_data select and is used to decide elimination period logic.

post_load_updates.update: UPDATE RPT_CLAIM_DTL_R SET D_CLAIM_AS_OF_DATE_R = gd_pacs_as_of_date_r WHERE n_yearmonth_r = gn_current_month
post_load_updates.derivable_at_insert_time: Yes; gd_pacs_as_of_date_r is fetched before the insert and could be written during the insert SELECT.

post_load_updates.update: FORALL updates setting v_has_associated_ltd_ind_r and v_has_associated_waiver_ind_r from rpt_associated_claims_mv_ssl-derived rows
post_load_updates.derivable_at_insert_time: Likely yes; rpt_associated_claims_mv_ssl is an available MV and could be left-joined in prc_get_cur_data, avoiding the separate update.

post_load_updates.update: FORALL updates setting d_claim_decision_date_r, n_claim_decision_days_r, v_turnaround_range1_r from aggregated rpt_fct_rpt_claim_summary_r results stored in rpt_claim_dtl_r_claimdec_GTT
post_load_updates.derivable_at_insert_time: Possibly (with more complex analytic/aggregation in the insert select or by joining a pre-aggregated source), but requires additional grouping/aggregation subquery — medium risk to fold.

main_steps_in_order: Insert job run-start log via pkg_grp_log_util.prc_insert_log
Call prc_upd_del_data: compute fiscal+2 date; either mark prior month rows inactive (UPDATE) or call prc_trunc_partition to truncate current month partition
prc_trunc_partition: ALTER TABLE ... TRUNCATE PARTITION PART_RPT_CLAIM_DTL_R_<gn_current_month> and rebuild PK indexes if unusable
Call prc_get_cur_data to OPEN a REF CURSOR for the large multi-join SELECT
In main: LOOP fetch REF CURSOR via BULK COLLECT LIMIT gn_bulk_coll_cnt and FORALL INSERT into rpt_claim_dtl_r; commit per batch
Close cursor
prc_insert_dummy_rec to insert a sentinel dummy record in rpt_claim_dtl_r; commit
prc_rebuild_indexes to rebuild non-PK unusable indexes
Update D_CLAIM_AS_OF_DATE_R in rpt_claim_dtl_r for current month
Call logging to mark job success/failure
intermediate_tables_created: rpt_claim_dtl_r_claimdec_GTT (GTT used in prc_upd_decision_cols as staging for aggregated decision rows)
staging_layers: rpt_associated_claims_mv_ssl (materialized view used as source for indicators)
Various MV/derived MV tables used inside prc_get_cur_data subselects
truncate_insert_patterns: Partition-level TRUNCATE of a partition PART_RPT_CLAIM_DTL_R_<gn_current_month> occurs when prc_upd_del_data decides so
Main load uses INSERT INTO rpt_claim_dtl_r VALUES (rowtype) from REF CURSOR -> BULK COLLECT -> FORALL insert

main_cursor.cursor_selects_from: A large SELECT that joins dim_grp_claim_dir_r (alias a) to many dims/facts/MVs (described in INPUT_DEPENDENCIES); prc_get_cur_data opens REF CURSOR
main_cursor.forall_updates_target: FORALL inserts into rpt_claim_dtl_r (the main insert target)
main_cursor.update_target_same_as_insert_target: N/A for main (FORALL is INSERT into target); subsequent FORALL updates in other procedures do update the same table (rpt_claim_dtl_r). The strongest same-table cursor->update pattern exists in prc_upd_wavier_ltd_ind_cols and prc_upd_decision_cols where cursors select from other objects (or GTT) and FORALL updates rpt_claim_dtl_r.
main_cursor.columns_set_by_cursor_update: In prc_upd_wavier_ltd_ind_cols: v_has_associated_ltd_ind_r & v_has_associated_waiver_ind_r (derivable by join); in prc_upd_decision_cols: d_claim_decision_date_r, n_claim_decision_days_r, v_turnaround_range1_r (derivable via aggregation over rpt_fct_rpt_claim_summary_r)

staging_table_analysis.reason: Inserted in prc_upd_decision_cols then immediately read by a cursor (cur_upd_dec_cols) to drive FORALL updates. Could be replaced by inline aggregation (CTE/subquery) feeding the FORALL or directly merged into a set-based UPDATE.

main.does: Orchestrates the whole load. Logs start, calls prc_upd_del_data, obtains REF CURSOR via prc_get_cur_data, bulk-loads into rpt_claim_dtl_r, calls prc_insert_dummy_rec, prc_rebuild_indexes, updates D_CLAIM_AS_OF_DATE_R, and logs completion.

prc_upd_del_data.does: Computes fiscal + 2-day threshold from DIM_TIME_R; if today equals that threshold, updates prior month's rows in rpt_claim_dtl_r to v_rpt_active_status_r='N'; otherwise sets gn_current_month and calls prc_trunc_partition to truncate the current partition.

prc_trunc_partition.does: Executes ALTER TABLE TRUNCATE PARTITION for the current partition and rebuilds any unusable PK indexes for RPT_CLAIM_DTL_R by querying ALL_INDEXES.

prc_get_cur_data.does: Opens REF CURSOR for a single large SELECT that joins many DIM/FCT/MV objects and produces the full rowtype for rpt_claim_dtl_r. Contains heavy CASE mappings, analytic RANK() and many left joins and subqueries.

prc_insert_dummy_rec.does: Inserts a single sentinel row into rpt_claim_dtl_r (batch/partition health), commits.

prc_rebuild_indexes.does: Rebuilds non-PK unusable indexes for RPT_CLAIM_DTL_R by iterating ALL_INDEXES and issuing ALTER INDEX ... REBUILD parallel 16 nologging.

prc_upd_wavier_ltd_ind_cols.does: Opens two cursors (one for LTD, one for WOP) selecting aggregated rows from rpt_associated_claims_mv_ssl grouped by claim keys; uses BULK COLLECT + FORALL to update v_has_associated_ltd_ind_r and v_has_associated_waiver_ind_r in rpt_claim_dtl_r for gn_current_month.

prc_upd_decision_cols.does: Builds aggregated rows (INSERT INTO rpt_claim_dtl_r_claimdec_GTT) from rpt_fct_rpt_claim_summary_r joined to rpt_claim_dtl_r to compute MAX(d_claim_decision_date_r) and decision days buckets; then BULK COLLECT + FORALL updates rpt_claim_dtl_r with the aggregated decision columns for gn_current_month.

procedure_level_flow.repeated_setup_cleanup_logic: Index rebuild scanning ALL_INDEXES appears in two places (prc_trunc_partition for PK_%, and prc_rebuild_indexes for non-PK indexes). Logging calls appear at the start of many procedures with same parameters - repeated pattern but typical for audit.

target_tables: rpt_claim_dtl_r_claimdec_GTT (GTT staging used only inside prc_upd_decision_cols)
OUTPUT_STRUCTURE.split_tables_exist: Yes — RPT_CLAIM_DTL_R is partitioned (procedure truncates PART_RPT_CLAIM_DTL_R_<gn_current_month>).
OUTPUT_STRUCTURE.union_used: No explicit UNIONs in the package body.
OUTPUT_STRUCTURE.output_data_grain: One row per claim/claim_coverage/claim_coverage_group for the reporting month (n_claim_sk_r, n_claim_coverage_sk_r, n_claim_coverage_group_sk_r, n_yearmonth_r).

PERFORMANCE_CHARACTERISTICS.parallelism_usage: Yes for index rebuilds (ALTER INDEX ... REBUILD parallel 16 nologging).
PERFORMANCE_CHARACTERISTICS.partition_usage: Yes — partition truncation used to remove prior month's data for the current partition before re-load.
PERFORMANCE_CHARACTERISTICS.bulk_operations: Yes — main load uses REF CURSOR -> BULK COLLECT -> FORALL INSERT; post-load updates use BULK COLLECT + FORALL with commits inside loops.
PERFORMANCE_CHARACTERISTICS.heavy_joins_or_subqueries: Yes — prc_get_cur_data SELECT contains many left joins, subselects, analytic rank(), and several MV/FACT reads. This is the heaviest SQL in the package.
potential_bottlenecks: The prc_get_cur_data SELECT (many joins across large DIM/FCT/MV objects) — likely the dominant CPU/IO cost.
Post-load FORALL updates that scan/modify the same target (rpt_claim_dtl_r) after the insert — extra I/O and potential for high redo/undo.
Frequent small commits (commit per bulk batch and commits inside update loops) can impede efficient redo/undo and prevent efficient direct-path operations.
Rebuilding indexes inside the load process (parallel 16) may be expensive and conflict with other maintenance windows.

duplicate_logic: Event-cause CASE mapping repeated twice in prc_get_cur_data (same large CASE -> code mapping block).
Index-rebuild patterns repeat in prc_trunc_partition and prc_rebuild_indexes (both query ALL_INDEXES and issue ALTER INDEX ... REBUILD).
OPTIMIZATION_SIGNALS.redundant_joins: prc_get_cur_data performs many LEFT JOINs and several derived-subquery MV joins; some MV lookups (e.g., MVW_PRODUCT_SK_LOOKUP_MIN_MV_SSL used twice as h and i) may be redundant or duplicative and could be consolidated into one derived table when appropriate.
OPTIMIZATION_SIGNALS.pass_through_transformations: A significant portion of the prc_get_cur_data SELECT is pass-through projection of DIM columns with minimal transformation — these are low-cost CPU but still cause repeated large JOINS.
staging_tables_that_can_be_removed: rpt_claim_dtl_r_claimdec_GTT — written then immediately read once; can be replaced by an inline aggregate (CTE or subquery) driving the update or by set-based MERGE.
Possible removal of separate UPDATE for D_CLAIM_AS_OF_DATE_R (value is available before insert and can be inserted directly).
repeated_transformation_patterns: Cursor -> BULK COLLECT -> FORALL update patterns used both in prc_upd_wavier_ltd_ind_cols and prc_upd_decision_cols (same looping/commit pattern). Consider consolidating templated helper.
OPTIMIZATION_SIGNALS.unnecessary_full_loads: If only partition for current month is truncated and reloaded, that is intended; however multiple subsequent updates create extra full-table (partition) scans — these updates are extra hops that could be merged into initial insert.
OPTIMIZATION_SIGNALS.high_cost_joins: Joins to large MVs/FACTs in prc_get_cur_data, especially the multiple MVW_PRODUCT_SK_LOOKUP_MIN_MV_SSL uses and CLAIM_TIER_WFAM_MV_TBL, payment_dates (FCT_CLAIM_PAYMENT_DETAIL_R_PMNT_MV_SSL), and DIM_GRP_CLAIM_ELIGIBILITY_R subselect with its own MAX() filter.

duplicate_SQL_blocks_across_child_proced.similarity_description: Two nearly identical cursor->FORALL update blocks differing only by source columns and constant values for which indicator to set.
duplicate_SQL_blocks_across_child_proced.consolidation_recommendation: Merge into a single parameterized routine that accepts source selection and target indicator mapping; reduces duplicated code and identical commit patterns.

duplicate_SQL_blocks_across_child_proced.similarity_description: Both query ALL_INDEXES and issue ALTER INDEX ... REBUILD; logic splits PK vs non-PK handling but is similar.
duplicate_SQL_blocks_across_child_proced.consolidation_recommendation: Unify index-rebuild logic into a single helper that accepts index name patterns or a mode (PK/non-PK) to avoid repeated ALL_INDEXES scans.

package_specific_signals.repeated_partition_index_maintenance: Index rebuild logic runs in multiple places; consider running a single consolidated rebuild after all DML to avoid repeated metadata scans.
package_specific_signals.repeated_logging_commit_patterns: Many procedures insert log rows and commit; centralize logging pattern if possible to reduce duplicated code and ensure consistent error handling.
package_specific_signals.merge_child_procedures_opportunities: prc_upd_wavier_ltd_ind_cols (two cursor loops) can be combined; prc_upd_decision_cols staging + update can be refactored to a set-based MERGE or single UPDATE from aggregated subquery; prc_rebuild_indexes and prc_trunc_partition index rebuilds can be centralized.

OPTIMIZATION_SIGNALS.direct_copy_vs_derived_logic: Much of the load is near-pass-through projections of DIM columns (direct copy). The heavy derived logic is limited to CASE mappings and rank() filtering. The presence of many post-load updates indicates opportunities to reduce hops where pass-through data is enriched later.

HOP_REDUCTION_OPPORTUNITIES.current_pattern: prc_get_cur_data (produce rows) -> main bulk insert into rpt_claim_dtl_r -> separate UPDATE (main) setting D_CLAIM_AS_OF_DATE_R
HOP_REDUCTION_OPPORTUNITIES.recommended_action: Set D_CLAIM_AS_OF_DATE_R in the prc_get_cur_data SELECT (gd_pacs_as_of_date_r is fetched prior to the insert) so the column is inserted directly; remove the separate UPDATE.
HOP_REDUCTION_OPPORTUNITIES.reason: Value is known before insert; folding avoids an extra write pass over the target partition and reduces I/O/redo.

HOP_REDUCTION_OPPORTUNITIES.current_pattern: Load then prc_upd_wavier_ltd_ind_cols cursor->FORALL updates reading rpt_associated_claims_mv_ssl then updating rpt_claim_dtl_r
HOP_REDUCTION_OPPORTUNITIES.recommended_action: Join rpt_associated_claims_mv_ssl (or its pre-aggregated projection) in prc_get_cur_data to produce v_has_associated_ltd_ind_r and v_has_associated_waiver_ind_r at insert time, eliminating the FORALL updates.
HOP_REDUCTION_OPPORTUNITIES.reason: Removes an entire read/update pass; source MV is available and can be left-joined; moderate SQL rewrite to ensure grouping/priority rules are preserved.

HOP_REDUCTION_OPPORTUNITIES.current_pattern: Aggregate decision columns into rpt_claim_dtl_r_claimdec_GTT then cursor->FORALL update of rpt_claim_dtl_r
HOP_REDUCTION_OPPORTUNITIES.recommended_action: Compute decision aggregates as a derived subquery/CTE and either (a) include them in the initial prc_get_cur_data select via a LEFT JOIN to the aggregate, or (b) perform a single set-based UPDATE using an aggregated subquery (no GTT and no cursor).
HOP_REDUCTION_OPPORTUNITIES.reason: Reduces writes and avoids temporary GTT and cursor movement; needs careful rewrite to replicate grouping and MAX logic.

HOP_REDUCTION_OPPORTUNITIES.current_pattern: Duplicated event-cause CASE mapping evaluated twice inside the same SELECT
HOP_REDUCTION_OPPORTUNITIES.recommended_action: Compute mapping once in an inline subexpression (WITH/CTE or nested subquery) and reference it for both uses in the SELECT.
HOP_REDUCTION_OPPORTUNITIES.reason: Simple refactor that reduces CPU and query complexity; no data semantics change.

HOP_REDUCTION_OPPORTUNITIES.current_pattern: Two similar cursor->FORALL loops inside prc_upd_wavier_ltd_ind_cols (LTD and WOP flows)
HOP_REDUCTION_OPPORTUNITIES.recommended_action: Combine into one parameterized loop/function (single cursor that returns the indicator type or a UNION of both source selects) and use a single FORALL update block.
HOP_REDUCTION_OPPORTUNITIES.reason: Reduces code duplication, easier maintenance, minimal runtime change.

HOP_REDUCTION_OPPORTUNITIES.current_pattern: Index rebuilds done in prc_trunc_partition (PK) and prc_rebuild_indexes (non-PK) with separate ALL_INDEXES scans
HOP_REDUCTION_OPPORTUNITIES.issue_type: redundant metadata scans and scattered maintenance
HOP_REDUCTION_OPPORTUNITIES.recommended_action: Consolidate index-rebuild logic into one post-load maintenance call that rebuilds all required indexes in one pass or consider scheduling rebuilds outside the package in a maintenance window.
HOP_REDUCTION_OPPORTUNITIES.reason: Reduces repeated ALL_INDEXES queries and centralizes heavy I/O operations.

structural_improvements: Expose a single public 'main' entry for the load (already present) and reduce the number of public procedures used only internally; mark helper procedures as private in the spec if possible.
Centralize logging and error-handling patterns into one reusable helper to remove repeated code blocks across procedures.
Consolidate index maintenance into a single helper or perform rebuilds outside of the ETL package (DBA-maintenance window).
SQL_optimization_ideas: Fold post-load updates into the initial insert: inject D_CLAIM_AS_OF_DATE_R, v_has_associated_* flags, and decision aggregates into the prc_get_cur_data SELECT via LEFT JOINs or aggregated subqueries.
